sections.html:
Pickerington straddles Fairfield and Franklin counties, so your tax bill, auditor and treasurer depend on which side of the line the parcel falls. It is the second-largest city in Fairfield County after Lancaster, yet a Pickerington address can still be billed by Franklin County. Look up your parcel number before listing so you know which county offices to call.

The July 2025 federal estimate is 26,333 people, 14.1% above the 2020 estimates base of 23,070. The city sits just east of Columbus, and growth since 2010 has come from annexation, development and people moving out from Columbus. The city went from 18,291 residents in 2010 to 23,094 in 2020, so buyers have newer subdivisions to compare against your house.

Pickerington is a family suburb with high owner occupancy and a high price point. Buyers who use a mortgage face an appraisal and a lender's review, so a house that needs repairs can stall in a retail sale. That is where as-is offers come in.

The 2020 count found 8,373 housing units, 5.5% of them vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3% and the rental vacancy rate 13.3%, so empty owner-occupied houses are scarce while rentals sit open more often. Newer subdivisions and the Olde Pickerington Village core give the city several different faces, so describe the part of town your house sits in. Families often search by school building, so name the schools that serve the street, and ask the district office to confirm attendance zones before you advertise them, since boundaries can change.

The city Building Department reviews plans, issues permits and inspects structures, and it is certified by the Ohio Board of Building Standards to enforce the 2019 Residential Code of Ohio and the 2024 Ohio Building Code. Contractor registration and building permits are filed on the city's OpenGov portal.

If past work on the house, such as a deck or finished basement, was done without a permit, sort it out before a buyer's inspector asks. Code Enforcement answers questions at 614-833-2204.

Code enforcement runs on complaints from residents. The city lists examples such as grass above 6 inches on a developed lot, piled debris and structures that are not maintained. Property maintenance and junk vehicle cases can take up to a month of legal steps before the owner gets a summons to Mayor's Court.

Vacant and abandoned homes must be registered. The annual fee is $150, due January 1 and received no later than January 31, with no proration. The registration names the mortgagee and, for an out-of-area owner, the local property manager. A buyer of a bank-owned house is told to check lien information with the zoning officer. Owners are also responsible for clearing sidewalks and storm drains under Section 660.05 of the Pickerington Codified Ordinances.

Fairfield County sets taxable value at 35% of market value, and any levy above the ten-mill limit needs a vote. Franklin County parcels follow the same state system but are administered from Columbus. Call the Fairfield County Auditor at 740-652-7020 or the Franklin County Treasurer at 614-525-3438 for your parcel's dates before you pick a closing day.

Franklin County owners can appeal the 2026 property value with the Auditor from November 20, 2026 through March 31, 2027. For Fairfield owners, the Auditor's Homestead program exempts the first $29,000 of value for qualifying owners and wants a wet-signed application filed within the year. The credit does not follow a homeowner to a new house, so a seller moving within the area must apply again at the new address.

sections.h2: What to do first for a quick sale
sections.html:
Start with the paperwork that only you can fix, then decide how to sell. A few checks save days later.

  • Find the parcel number and confirm whether Fairfield or Franklin County bills it.
  • Ask the Building Department about any permit that was never closed for a deck, basement or addition.
  • Check whether a vacant house still needs its annual $150 registration and whether a lien exists.
  • Find out if you hold a Homestead credit, since Fairfield County says it does not transfer to a new home.
  • Gather the school names that serve the street, the age of the roof and furnace, and any HOA rules.

With those answers in hand, a listing agent, a direct buyer or the county offices can each respond faster, and you can compare offers on the same facts.

sections.h2: Fees and dates to write down
sections.html:
• Vacant or abandoned home registration: $150 a year, due by January 31 (City of Pickerington).
  • Homestead value exempted: the first $29,000 (Fairfield County Auditor).
  • Franklin County value appeal for tax year 2026: November 20, 2026 to March 31, 2027 (Franklin County Auditor).

Put these on one page next to your parcel number and the phone numbers above. When a buyer, a title company or an inspector asks a question, you can answer it or point to the right office right away.

If the house is vacant, the vacant registration is the item most likely to cost you money by surprise. It is due each January 1 with no proration, so a house that sits empty into the new year owes the full amount even if it sells in February. Ask the zoning officer whether a lien is on file, and keep sidewalks and storm drains clear while the house is on the market, since the owner is responsible for both.

sections.h2: Who should consider a cash sale?
sections.html:
Cash suits a seller who values a firm closing date over squeezing out extra price. At these values a lender will require an appraisal, and a buyer's inspection can reopen the price when the roof is old or a deck lacks a permit.

Direct buyers usually take the property in current condition, which helps with an inherited house, a rental after a tenant leaves or a vacant house that needs registering. Request written offers from more than one buyer and ask who pays closing costs. A cash sale still has to deal with the county your parcel sits in, so confirm whether Fairfield or Franklin handles the deed and the tax proration before you accept. Ask the buyer to take on any open permit, and get the closing date in the contract. If the house is empty, finish the vacant registration first so a city notice does not appear halfway through the sale.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax on a Pickerington house?
faqs.a: It is Fairfield or Franklin County depending on the parcel, since the city spans both. Look up your parcel number and ask that county's treasurer for the due dates.

faqs.q: Does Pickerington require me to register a vacant house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires registration of abandoned or vacant homes with an annual fee of $150, due January 1 and received by January 31 each year.

faqs.q: How big is the Fairfield County Homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Qualifying owners can exempt the first $29,000 of appraised value. The form needs a wet signature and must be filed within the year the credit is sought.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pickerington house with an unpermitted deck?
faqs.a: You can, but a buyer's inspector may find it. The Building Department explains the permit steps, and a direct buyer may take the house as is.
The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 26,333 residents, up from 23,070 in April 2020. Households average 2.89 people.
